Dhurandhar: The Revenge Opens To a Monster ₹115 Crore in 36 Hours. Biggest Hindi Opener. Ever.

Eight days before release, Dhurandhar 2 has destroyed every Bollywood premiere record ever set. Stree 2 is gone. Pawan Kalyan's OG at ₹25 Cr is the last wall standing — and it's crumbling by the hour.

By The Boxoffy Team · Originally Mar 9, 2026 · Last Updated Mar 20, 2026 — Day 1 Confirmed · Sources: Sacnilk · Pinkvilla · Koimoi · THR India · Venky BO

When advance booking opened on March 7, the trade gave Dhurandhar 2 a two-part challenge: first break Stree 2's ₹8.75 crore Bollywood premiere record, then hunt Pawan Kalyan's OG — the ₹25 crore all-India premiere record, the highest any Indian film has ever earned from paid premieres alone. Both records now belong to Dhurandhar: The Revenge. By March 17, premiere gross stands at ₹37.31 crore (with blocks), ₹33+ crore real tickets — across 6.86 lakh premiere tickets in 9,000+ shows. The combined premiere + Day 1 advance has crossed ₹50 crore gross in India. The OG record is gone. The worldwide advance is approaching ₹60 crore before regular show bookings have even opened in India.

The pace has been extraordinary. Premiere tickets crossed 6.86 lakh by March 17, with 9,000+ premiere shows across India. The Day 1 pre-sales (excluding previews) stand at ₹24.50 crore gross across 6.25 lakh tickets in 13,000+ shows. The Hindi 2D version remains the primary engine at an ATP of ₹414, but South pricing has opened a volume play — the cheapest ticket is ₹59 at AGS Cinemas in Chennai, while Mumbai's INOX Megaplex Recliner Prime hits ₹2,900. Trade analyst Taran Adarsh confirmed the film was clocking 7,500 to 10,000 tickets per hour on BookMyShow when premiere bookings first went live — a pace rarely seen for Indian films.

“Films like Dhurandhar: The Revenge are made for the scale, sound and emotion that only cinemas can deliver. We have already surpassed 150,000 tickets in advance sales at PVR INOX alone.”
Gautam Dutta, CEO PVR INOX — to Variety India, March 11, 2026

The national chains are at capacity. PVR INOX CEO Gautam Dutta called the response a "big screen celebration" and confirmed 1.5 lakh+ tickets in PVR INOX chains alone. Wednesday March 18 PLF shows across the US and Canada have sold out at multiple locations (Variety). North America advance for the opening weekend is nearing $2 million across 678 locations — on track to surpass several pan-India films' overseas OW totals (Sacnilk). In India, 5,00,000 BMS users have marked interest for the sequel — Dhurandhar 1 sold 1.3 crore tickets on BMS, the highest for any Hindi film on the platform.

The overseas picture is historic for a Hindi film. The US premiere pre-sales alone crossed $982,374 across 678 locations by mid-March, surpassing Animal's all-time Bollywood US premiere record. North America opening weekend advance is approaching $2M. The worldwide advance total — India + overseas — is around ₹60 crore gross, and this is before regular admission bookings have opened in India. When they do, the ₹100 crore combined premiere+Day 1 advance target becomes realistic.

New: Yami Gautam confirmed in cast. Runtime: 3 hrs 55 mins. Regular India show bookings not yet open — all figures above are premiere-only advance.

The Boxoffy Call
₹115 Crore ✓ Confirmed
India Net Actual  ·  D0 ₹43 Cr + D1 ₹72 Cr  ·  BPREDICT v1 Called ₹110 Cr  ·  Range ₹101–122 Cr  ·  Actual: Within Range ✓

Every source you'll read today has a number between ₹97 Cr and ₹125 Cr. Pinkvilla — the most respected pre-release tracker — has landed at ₹105 Cr. We're at ₹110 Cr. Here's why, plainly.

The Day 1 number has two parts: the premiere on March 18 (evening shows only) and the full release on March 19. The premiere has already sold ₹35.99 crore in advance — real money in the bank before a single show begins. With premium-format IMAX and Dolby shows sold out across Mumbai, Delhi and Hyderabad, and limited remaining seats, we expect premiere collections to close around ₹36–37 crore net.

The opening day is the harder call. We anchor against Jawan's ₹64 crore opening — the highest Day 1 for a Hindi film before this — and build upward from three things D2 has that Jawan didn't.

Eid + Gudi Padwa + Ugadi on the same day. Jawan released on a regular Wednesday. D2 has the rarest festive combination in years — Eid sends North India occupancy up 10–14 points, while the Gudi Padwa and Ugadi state holidays put Maharashtra, Andhra Pradesh and Telangana on school-and-office shutdowns simultaneously. There is no comparable precedent.

1,500 more screens. D2 opens on 5,500 screens versus Jawan's 4,000. On a packed holiday, every extra screen with a full house is roughly ₹4–6 lakh in revenue. At 1,500 additional screens that's ₹6–9 crore before any other factor.

Five languages. Jawan was primarily a Hindi release. D2 adds Telugu, Tamil, Kannada and Malayalam — circuits whose advance data (33,000+ Telugu tickets, 28,000+ Tamil tickets already sold) adds another ₹7–8 crore that a Hindi-only model simply misses. That's precisely where our ₹5 crore gap with Pinkvilla comes from.

The one drag is runtime. At 3 hours 49 minutes, each screen fits about 3.8 shows per day instead of the usual 5–6. That's a real capacity cut, especially at single screens where a 4-hour film can't run three commercial shows in a day. We've reduced our screen arithmetic accordingly.

Boxoffy Verdict · Mar 20, 2026 · Day 1 Confirmed ✅

The Reckoning is done. Day 0: ₹43 Cr nett — the biggest premiere in Indian cinema history. Day 1: ₹72 Cr nett — the biggest opening day for a Hindi film in history, beating Jawan's ₹64 Cr on holiday by ₹8 Cr on a non-holiday Thursday. Combined D0+D1: ₹115 Crore. BPREDICT v1 called ₹110 Cr (range ₹101–122 Cr) — actual landed at ₹115 Cr, within range, error +4.5%. The model's structural logic was right: festive stacking + five-language release + 5,500 screens drove the outperformance. WW D0+D1 gross: ₹159 Cr. NA premiere: $1.43M (Venky BO, 705 locations). Weekend projection: ₹350–380 Cr India nett. The Dhurandhar franchise has officially entered a league of its own.
